# CPU-Quine instruction set

<!-- GENERATED by `python3 -m quine.isadoc` from quine/arch.py; do not edit. -->

16-bit words, word addressed.  Registers A, X, Y (16 bits), SP (8), PC (15), flags Z, N, C.
Internal: IR (16), MU (2-bit microstate).  Every flip-flop resets to zero.

## Encoding

| Form | Bits | Operand word |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Memory | `1 oooo mm s 00000000`: op, mode (imm, abs, abs+X, abs+Y), space (0 ROM, 1 RAM) | always |
| Other | `0 ppppp aaaaaaaaaa`: op, 10-bit signed branch offset from the next word | JMP, JSR, JMPX |

Stores always write RAM and treat the immediate mode as absolute.  Encodings with no
instruction (op 28) execute as a 3-cycle no-op.  The opcode's high byte is the stepper's
dispatch index.

## Memory instructions

`M` is the operand (immediate) or the word at operand (+X or +Y) in the selected space.

| Op | Code | Cycles (imm / abs) | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| LDA | `10000` | 3 / 4 | A <- M; Z,N |
| LDX | `10001` | 3 / 4 | X <- M; Z,N |
| LDY | `10010` | 3 / 4 | Y <- M; Z,N |
| STA | `10011` | 4 / 4 | M <- A (RAM) |
| STX | `10100` | 4 / 4 | M <- X (RAM) |
| STY | `10101` | 4 / 4 | M <- Y (RAM) |
| ADD | `10110` | 3 / 4 | A <- A + M; Z,N,C |
| ADC | `10111` | 3 / 4 | A <- A + M + C; Z,N,C |
| SUB | `11000` | 3 / 4 | A <- A - M (C = no borrow); Z,N,C |
| SBC | `11001` | 3 / 4 | A <- A + ~M + C; Z,N,C |
| AND | `11010` | 3 / 4 | A <- A & M; Z,N |
| OR | `11011` | 3 / 4 | A <- A \| M; Z,N |
| XOR | `11100` | 3 / 4 | A <- A ^ M; Z,N |
| CMP | `11101` | 3 / 4 | A - M; Z,N,C |
| CPX | `11110` | 3 / 4 | X - M; Z,N,C |
| CPY | `11111` | 3 / 4 | Y - M; Z,N,C |

## Other instructions

| Op | Code | Cycles | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| BRA | `000000` | 3 | branch always |
| BEQ | `000001` | 3 | branch if Z |
| BNE | `000010` | 3 | branch if not Z |
| BCS | `000011` | 3 | branch if C |
| BCC | `000100` | 3 | branch if not C |
| BMI | `000101` | 3 | branch if N |
| BPL | `000110` | 3 | branch if not N |
| DBNE | `000111` | 4 | X <- X - 1; branch if X != 0 (no flags) |
| SHL | `001000` | 3 | C <- A[15], A <- A << 1; Z,N |
| SHR | `001001` | 3 | C <- A[0], A <- A >> 1; Z,N |
| ROL | `001010` | 3 | A <- {A[14:0], C}, C <- A[15]; Z,N |
| ROR | `001011` | 3 | A <- {C, A[15:1]}, C <- A[0]; Z,N |
| SWAB | `001100` | 3 | A <- {A[7:0], A[15:8]}; Z,N |
| TAX | `001101` | 3 | X <- A; Z,N |
| TAY | `001110` | 3 | Y <- A; Z,N |
| TXA | `001111` | 3 | A <- X; Z,N |
| TYA | `010000` | 3 | A <- Y; Z,N |
| TSX | `010001` | 3 | X <- SP; Z,N |
| TXS | `010010` | 3 | SP <- X[7:0] |
| INX | `010011` | 3 | X <- X + 1; Z,N |
| INY | `010100` | 3 | Y <- Y + 1; Z,N |
| DEX | `010101` | 3 | X <- X - 1; Z,N |
| DEY | `010110` | 3 | Y <- Y - 1; Z,N |
| CLC | `010111` | 3 | C <- 0 |
| SEC | `011000` | 3 | C <- 1 |
| PHA | `011001` | 4 | RAM[$0200+SP] <- A; SP <- SP - 1 |
| PLA | `011010` | 4 | SP <- SP + 1; A <- RAM[$0200+SP]; Z,N |
| RTS | `011011` | 4 | SP <- SP + 1; PC <- RAM[$0200+SP] |
| JMP | `011101` | 3 | PC <- operand |
| JSR | `011110` | 4 | RAM[$0200+SP] <- return address; SP <- SP - 1; PC <- operand |
| JMPX | `011111` | 4 | PC <- ROM[operand + X] (jump table) |

## Timing

Every instruction starts with a fetch cycle (drive PC, PC += 1) and a decode cycle
(IR <= RDATA, PC += 1 if the opcode has an operand word).  Its last cycle drives the
address of the next instruction in ROM space, so at every instruction boundary
RDATA equals ROM[PC].

## Memory

| Space | Addresses | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ROM | 32K words | reads use address bits [14:0]; never written |
| RAM | $0000-$7FFF | 128 pages of 256 words; cleared by the reset controller |
| I/O | $FFFE, $FFFF | write-only: debug port, self-reset; reads above $7FFF return 0 |

The address driven in cycle t is read at the rising edge ending cycle t and appears
on RDATA in cycle t+1.  A read happens every cycle; a write is read-first.
